summary: Trout Mountain's 80-ft tower was built in 2020 by The Nature Conservancy from salvaged parts of a 1940s Alabama tower, replacing a fire tower closed in the 1970s.

events.note: Maine Memory caption says the lookout station moved to Trout Mountain; the caption sits beside a Black Cat Mountain photo, so the link to this summit is probable, not proven
The 120-ft Alabama tower, said to date from the 1940s, was in use until 2017, when Davana bought it
Erected by The Nature Conservancy with Davana LLC from salvaged parts; replaced a fire tower closed in the 1970s

corrections.why: The parenthetical describes a 2020 rebuild that reuses salvaged Alabama parts, not a tower moved intact; the origin is better told in events and the story

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Conservancy gives the summit as 1,409 ft and Davana gives 1,427 ft; no source settles it, so the story reports both
The FFLA label says relocated from Alabama; the Conservancy and the builder describe a 2020 rebuild that reuses salvaged Alabama parts. The 'relocated' event is best read as the origin of the parts

The FFLA lists an older Trout Mountain tower as Gone at 45.80191, -68.84884; the 2020 structure is listed as standing at 45.80238, -68.85003, about 106 m away by my calculation. The Conservancy says the old tower lies in ruins

notes_for_editor: Built and rebuilt dates (2020) agree across three sources. The 1931 station move rests on a Maine Memory caption that sits beside a Black Cat Mountain photo, so it may refer to another structure. The closure is only given as 'the 1970s'; no source gives a year. The 120-ft height, the 1940s date and the Alabama origin rest on Davana's page alone, and the Conservancy only says 'Alabama'. Name correction needs human sign-off. Summit elevation disagrees (1,409 vs 1,427 ft). Sources treat the tower as open to hikers, but none states a formal public-access rule for the tower itself.
